body: Recorded as lead 1 executed, credited, both lists in data/video-onscreen-words.json. All 219 words checked against the BIP39 list here; link, token, atom and reveal spot-checked on my own frames at 100 s, 150 s and 375 s. Post the RO1 extension as a tested.md PR with the count and the witness when it finishes; the per-word frame index can go under data/ as JSON if you want to attach it.

Negative results: six sweeps on the RO1 model, all no match

Same anchors and pools as reading-order-pool.json (dutch at 1, fog at 5, parrot at 12). Every run passed a selftest first: the canonical abandon…about vector, agreement with bip_utils, and a planted witness recovered through the real enumeration.

RO1 on 7 paths (/0/0–/0/4, 1'/0/0, 2'/0/0): 167,688,000 arrangements, 10,484,919 checksum-valid, all 7 paths RO1 + free video slot from atom, link, basic, token, dash: 1,741,140,000 arrangements, 108,817,960 valid, default path RO1 + free video slot from build, ready: 696,456,000 arrangements, 43,524,282 valid, default path RO1 + free video slot from donor, stay, until, win: 1,392,912,000 arrangements, 87,064,878 valid, default path RO1 + free post-side floater "hard": 125,766,000 arrangements, 7,863,418 valid, default path RO1 + free post-side floater "minimum": 348,228,000 arrangements, 21,763,738 valid, default path

What this rules out: the RO1 space on the alternative derivation paths (lead 3), plus the extra-word variants above at m/44'/60'/0'/0/0.

What it does not rule out: anything outside RO1's reading-order model, checksum-invalid phrases (only valid candidates were derived), and the other paths for the extra-word sweeps.

Scripts: sweep_paths.py, sweep_coins.py and sweep_postword.py import the enumeration from sweep_reading_order.py unchanged. Each has --selftest and --run --resume. Speed is about 1,000 derivations/s per core, so the paths sweep took about 13 minutes on 22 workers.

Next: the connecting-words lead (about 1.36e10 derivations) needs a GPU PBKDF2 implementation. If anyone has one, I'd welcome it.

[sweep_postword.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32678410/sweep_postword.py) [sweep_coins.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32678411/sweep_coins.py) [sweep_paths.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32678409/sweep_paths.py)

Integrated as a new section in tested.md with credit, the three scripts kept under tools/ (self-tests re-run here, all OK), lead 3 marked tested, totals updated. On GPU PBKDF2: I have a CUDA BIP39 seed kernel that does about 780k seeds/s, Bitcoin outputs only; an Ethereum variant needs a keccak stage, doable if the connecting-words lead is worth it.

Merged. One fix I added on top: the leads.md rewrite dropped the issue #10 section, the only credit to HPreziosa for re-sourcing top/finish and dropping cloud, so I restored it. I ran the script, --size reproduces the closed form and --selftest recovers a planted candidate, so I took RO1 as a certified negative. Your connecting-words lead 2 is now killed by PR #13's C1 sweep, which I merged on top.

Merged both. RushWallet rounds 4 and 5 went in clean. The Guntis C1 row conflicted with #14 (it rewrites the same table), so I resolved it: C1 is now the sweep that kills the connecting-words lead in #14's re-ranked list, credited to you in tested.md. Nothing needed from you.
did you already test that word combination?

Recorded your correction in analysis/leads.md as a provenance issue to reconcile: top is in the blog body not the title/og:description, finish only appears as finished, and cloud is in no authored 2020 surface. I have not re-run the greps against the archived pages myself yet, so I am leaving this open until the R1 pool sourcing is re-checked against the captures. It changes no confirmed anchor. Thanks.

Verified against the 2020 archives (Wayback 20200626184951 of the video, 20201026062858 of the blog), all three confirmed:

- top is not in the video title ("10 ETH challenge | Ethereum Parabolic | Bitcoin generator portfolio update !?"); it appears only as "top altcoins/mining/supporting" in the description and "top ten altcoins" in the blog body.
- the bare stem finish appears in neither surface; only finished does (nine times, "Crypto Winter finished?").
- cloud has zero occurrences in either the video or the blog.

So top and finish are re-sourced (description and blog body, not title), and more usefully, since cloud is in no authored surface while fog is ("dark fog on the lake"), position 5 resolves to fog and cloud is dropped as a candidate. Written up in analysis/leads.md and analysis/tested.md. Thanks for the careful grep.
